individuals.treatment_summary: Valproate begun but associated with lethargy (worsening later attributed to valproate given the metabolic diagnosis); then lamotrigine with fair seizure control. Lives in a group home.
individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: Urine organic acids showed 4-hydroxybutyric aciduria; enzymatic quantification of SSADH activity in leucocytes confirmed the diagnosis.

phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail: Wechsler Intelligence Scales for Children: verbal 55, performance 65

phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated: deficient adaptive behaviors on the Vineland Adaptive Behavioral Scales
mild background slowing during wakefulness on EEG
intermittent generalized spike-wave discharges that were activated during sleep
increased T2-weighted signal in the globus pallidus

individuals.cause_of_death: SUDEP (died with a diagnosis of SUDEP; death at age nineteen after escalating convulsive seizure activity)
individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: Diagnosis made retrospectively following the confirmed diagnosis in her living sister; the homozygous Aldh5A1 p.Gly409Asp mutation found in the sister was subsequently confirmed in the decedent.
individuals.source_reference_in_review: [15] Knerr I, Gibson KM, Murdoch G, et al, 2010, Neuropathology in succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency, Pediatr Neurol PMID:20304328

variants.parental_testing_statement: Both parents were confirmed as heterozygote carriers.

phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated: seizure onset at age thirteen years
striking discoloration of the globus pallidi
hyperemia and granular perivascular calcification of the globus pallidus and superior colliculus
phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail: microscopic examination; consistent with chronic excitotoxic injury

phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated: significant neuronal loss or gliosis of CA1 of the hippocampus

individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis: Subsequent diagnosis of SSADH deficiency after presenting with seizures; pathogenic homozygous Aldh5A1 mutation (p.Gly409Asp) detected.

individuals.individual_label_in_paper: 2 ½-year-old boy (case report available as an abstract [33])
individuals.treatment_summary: Taurine 4 grams/day (~200 mg/kg) over one year in a boy described as a 2 ½-year-old boy; reported to improve gait, coordination and energy; at 9 months teachers reported improved behavior, peer interactions, increased level of activity and coordination; at 12 months MRI interpreted as improved; higher doses associated with insomnia; no correlation between improved behavior and urine GHB levels. Uncontrolled, unblinded.
